text:
Incident Bot: Pager triggered: GPU memory pressure detected in pool p-nyc-02. severity=P1. metric=nvml.mem.used_pct > 92% for 3m. submitting pager to oncall rota -> PD incident PD-94721.
PagerDuty: PD-94721 created and notified -> escalation policy: gpu-oncall.
jamie (oncall): acked PD-94721 :raised_hand: taking lead. quick status?
jamie (oncall): checking cluster heatmap, running `rhc gpu list -p p-nyc-02 --format=json`
sasha: reported similar noise earlier this morning on p-nyc-01, may be correlated.
jamie (oncall): logs from one affected instance ->
```
[2025-03-07T02:13:45Z] runtime: allocate_cuda(0) failed: out of memory
[2025-03-07T02:13:46Z] kv-cache: evicting 12 shards to free 3.2GB
[2025-03-07T02:13:46Z] runtime: fallback to smaller model variant: redwood-7b-v2-qlora
```
runtime-bot: autoscaler attempted burst+preemptive-evict on p-nyc-02, 2/4 requests rejected due to pool exhaustion.
lee: are any customer-facing requests failing, or just internal reroutes?
maria-sre: CC @jamie looking at ingress logs — 1% of requests to redwood-7b returned 503 between 02:12-02:15 UTC, mainly from tenant org:fin-edge-prod.
jamie (oncall): mark customer impact: partial errors for a small subset of requests -> probable user-visible errors. paging product for potential P1 customer outreach.
jamie (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) scale up p-nyc-02 with one extra GPU node 2) temporarily increase kv-cache eviction threshold 3) pin noisy jobs to lower priority queue
sasha: I'm on step 1, creating node: `infractl pool add-node --pool p-nyc-02 --instance g5.2xlarge --reason "oom surge"`
sasha: node request submitted, ETA ~ 90s to attach.
lee: while we wait, can we drain one noisy worker? `rhc task list --pool p-nyc-02 | grep heavy`
maria-sre: logs show a few long-running rerank jobs from partner:ads-batch; throttling them now.
jamie (oncall): throttled 3 jobs, applied lower QoS. monitoring memory usage.
runtime-bot: pool p-nyc-02 memory usage dropping from 94% -> 88% after throttles. evictions rate down.
PagerDuty: PD-94721 acknowledged by jamie (oncall). escalation paused.
jamie (oncall): thanks @sasha for the node. once new node ready we should rebalance KV cache and restart runtime on the hotspot instance. plan to run rolling restart of 3 pods with `kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-p-nyc-02 -n inference --grace-period=60`
sasha: new node attached: instance-id i-0c12345 attached to p-nyc-02. starting rebalance now.
jamie (oncall): rebalance kicked off: `kvrebalance --src p-nyc-02 --dst p-nyc-02 --parallel 6` (internal cmd). watching.
runtime-bot: kvrebalance progress: 22% complete.
maria-sre: customer impact update: errors for org:fin-edge-prod reduced to 0.2% in last 3m, alerting product.
lee: any sign of model switchovers causing higher mem usage? recent deploy?
jamie (oncall): checked deploys: no model deploys in the last 24h. desktop payload for ads-batch increased traffic ~x3; looks like load spike rather than regression.
sasha: rebalance completed, starting rolling restarts on 3 hotspot pods.
runtime-bot: rolling restart step 1/3 complete. pod runtime-p-nyc-02-5 restarted -> back to ready.
runtime-bot: rolling restart complete. memory stable at 66%-72% across pool. evictions stopped.
jamie (oncall): closing mitigation: scaled pool +1, throttled heavy jobs, rebalanced KV cache, rolled restarts. will keep PD open until we validate 30m.
PagerDuty: PD-94721 status -> acknowledged -> monitoring.
maria-sre: prepping post-incident note for customers impacted (org:fin-edge-prod). adding observability graphs, error samples.
lee: follow-up actions: - add autoscale headroom for p-nyc pools during regional business hours - add alert rule for sustained nvml.mem.used_pct > 90% for 5m - throttle signature for ads-batch rerank jobs to avoid OOM cascade
jamie (oncall): definitely. i'll create the follow-up tickets and tag @oncall-leads.
sasha: nice work everyone. reassign PD to oncall rotation for monitoring: PD-94721 -> open.
jamie (oncall): handing off monitoring to @lee in 15m. I will update runbook with sequence used.
lee: acked handoff. I'll watch for 30m.
Incident Bot: Note: runbook used -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-memory-pressure.incident.
jamie (oncall): resolved for now — marking thread as stable. final notes: root cause likely transient traffic surge + insufficient headroom on p-nyc-02; no code regression. follow-ups created. :white_check_mark:
